skills.title: Instrument Orientation
skills.summary: Identify the parts of the instrument and settle into a safe, repeatable playing position.

skills.title: Steady Pulse
skills.summary: Hold an even quarter-note pulse against a count, without drifting faster or slower.

skills.title: Sustained Tone
skills.summary: Produce a single note that stays even in pitch and volume for its whole length.

skills.title: Strumming
skills.summary: Sound several strings together in a repeating rhythmic pattern, keeping the pulse in the strumming arm.

skills.title: Sight-Reading Basics
skills.summary: Read pitch and duration from notation accurately enough to play a short unseen passage.

skills.title: Tempo Control
skills.summary: Hold a chosen tempo through a passage, and change tempo deliberately rather than by drifting.

skills.title: First Melody
skills.summary: Play a short prepared melody from start to finish with correct notes and steady timing.

suggested_edges.rationale: Keeping time on an instrument presupposes holding it in a repeatable way.
A steady tone comes from a stable setup before it comes from anything else.
A strum pattern is a pulse expressed by the playing arm.
Note values are durations against a pulse; without one they are only shapes.
Holding a chosen tempo presupposes holding a pulse at all.
A melody is a sequence of tones, and each one has to be worth hearing.
A prepared melody is read before it is performed.
A performed melody has to hold its tempo from start to finish.
